subject: general
question: Between the ages of six and fourteen, parents or guardians should provide opportunities for their children's education. When did this become a part of the right to education legislation?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2009**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The 86th amendment provided legislation for the Right to Education Act (RTE) between the ages of six and fourteen, parents or guardians should provide opportunities for their children's education in 2009.

 
 
• It mandated the R**ight of children to free and compulsory education till the completion of elementary education in a neighbourhood school.**
 
• **25% reservation for SCs and STs, socially Backward Class and Differently abled children.**
 
• **No child shall be liable to pay any kind of fee or charges or expenses which may prevent him or her from pursuing and completing elementary education.**
 
• **It lays down standards for Pupil-Teacher Ratios,** infrastructure, school-working days, teacher-working hours etc.
 
• It provides provisions for the appointment of appropriately trained teachers.
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• The Right to Education for all between 6 and 14 years of age has been included in Article 21-A of Fundamental Rights in the Constitution of India.
 
• It was included in the Constitution through the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.
 
• It provides the free and compulsory education of all children in the age group of six to fourteen years as a Fundamental Right.
 
• In 1993, the Judgment of SC in the Unnikrishnan vs State of Andhra Pradesh & Others held that *Education is a fundamental right under Article 21*.
